mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and lowering expected equity valuations, which negatively impacts the 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a sustained manner over 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-test), or FEDFUNDS does not remain above 4% for 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor market activity) coinciding with UNRATE below 6% suggests a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 130,000 and UNRATE < 6% simultaneously
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS > 130,000 and UNRATE < 6% hold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (residential construction) accompanied by a decline in INDPRO (industrial production) indicates shifting demand toward housing, which supports equity valuations and yields positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the HOUST/INDPRO pattern persists (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side conditions, lowering market capacity and pushing up S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months by >2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline period.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL rising faster than GDP deflator (implied by GDPC1) indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady but eroding future equity real returns, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate > GDPC1 growth rate by >0.5 percentage points over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the inflation gap persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit expectations, which produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE < 4% period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in PAYEMS (>140,000) and HOUST (>600) indicates robust consumer and housing demand, which elevates equity risk premiums and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 140,000 and HOUST > 600 in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when both indicators meet the threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of over 10% for two consecutive months suggests weak consumer demand, lowering growth expectations and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months by >10%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the RSAFS decline.
